subject: rain

identity.evidence: The nine-stroke sparse rain motif survives through the six phases, including the five upper strokes, four lower strokes, characteristic bent lower strokes, uneven lengths and varied slants. Lower strokes shorten in the later phases, but the drawing continues to read as the same original motif.

poses.evidence: As procedural rain-field phases, the six keys visibly progress downward, shorten the low strokes, and reseed higher in key six. This is a plausible shorthand for the source continuous falling rain. The source does not support identifying these as six observations of particular tracked drops, and this verdict makes no such claim.

protect: Uneven original lengths, slants and bent strokes
Downward phase progression and wet-road held background
scope: Only design.png, first six board-v1 tiles and held-background tile seven, selected 16-frame and six-key source contact sheets were inspected. This is still-key plausibility only; no rendered motion was reviewed.
